title: One write: from the key to three Availability Zones
claim: A write lands in the partition that the key's hash picks, and DynamoDB replicates it across three Availability Zones.
alt: A sequence with four participants: an application, DynamoDB, one partition, and its copies in three Availability Zones. The application sends a write with the item's key. DynamoDB hashes the partition key and picks the partition. The partition stores the item in three zones. DynamoDB returns success. A later read is eventually consistent unless it asks for a strong read.

messages.label: Write item
messages.say: The application sends a write that holds the item's primary key.

messages.label: Hash picks it
messages.say: DynamoDB feeds the partition key value into an internal hash function, which determines the partition.

messages.label: Sync copy
messages.say: DynamoDB synchronously replicates the item across three Availability Zones.

messages.label: Success
messages.say: When the write returns HTTP 200 (OK), it has been durably persisted.

messages.label: Later read
messages.say: Eventually consistent is the default for a later read; a strongly consistent read returns the most up-to-date data.
